key_insight: Adding more images to VLM inputs exposes systematic, controllable failure modes—errors in aggregation, cross-image coreference, and distractor handling increase with image count. MIMIC pinpoints these weaknesses and their causes.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of a rigorous, controlled benchmark and analysis for multi-image vision-language understanding, diagnosing why and how LVLMs fail when reasoning over multiple images.
method: Introduce MIMIC: a controlled benchmark of multi-image tasks with systematic variations (relevance, distractors, ordering, cross-image references) and fine-grained annotations.
Run controlled probes and ablations across multiple LVLMs to quantify performance degradation as image count/complexity increases and to categorize error types.
Define metrics and a failure-mode taxonomy to attribute errors to specific causes (aggregation, alignment, hallucination, attention dilution) and measure sensitivity to task factors.
impact: Gives researchers and engineers a practical diagnostic tool and taxonomy to evaluate, compare, and improve multi-image reasoning in VLMs—guiding dataset design, model architectures, and mitigation strategies.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram of MIMIC: input (N images + prompt) → controlled perturbations → model → labeled error categories
Bar chart or line plot showing error rate vs. number of images across models (demonstrating scaling failure)
Stacked chart or heatmap of failure-mode frequencies (aggregation, coreference, distractors, hallucination) per model and per task type
Side-by-side example panels: (a) multi-image prompt, (b) correct reasoning annotation, (c) common model failure with explanation
paper_title: More Images, More Problems? A Controlled Analysis of VLM Failure Modes
paper_authors: Anurag Das, Adrian Bulat, Alberto Baldrati, Ioannis Maniadis Metaxas, Bernt Schiele
